name: Learn basic embroidery
blurb: Six stitches cover most designs. Embroidery needs almost no equipment, travels well, and turns a plain shirt or tote into something personal in an evening.
gear: Stranded cotton floss and embroidery needles
Cotton fabric and a water-soluble marker
steps: Learn to hoop the fabric drum-tight and to separate floss strands — most designs use two or three of the six.
Learn the core stitches: running, back, stem, satin, French knot and lazy daisy.
Learn to start and finish without knots, using a waste knot or weaving under existing stitches.
Transfer a simple design and outline it in back stitch.
Fill shapes with satin stitch, keeping the strands flat and parallel — this is where neatness shows.
Finish the back tidily and mount or wear the piece.
tips: Puckered fabric means your tension is too tight or the hoop was slack.
French knots collapse when you let go of the thread tension. Keep it taut as you pull through.
proof: A finished piece using at least four stitches, with a back tidy enough to show someone.
